Stages of dedupe() and summarize_duplicates()

Source: R/utils-dedupe.R
sort_for_dedupe.Rd

Internal helpers that dedupe() and summarize_duplicates() run in order, so each exported function reads as a short pipeline.

Usage

sort_for_dedupe(
  data,
  facility_col,
  visit_col,
  order_by_quo,
  keep,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

keep_group_rows(data, fac_col_str, visit_col_str, keep)

count_visit_row_groups(data_clean, fac_col_str, visit_col_str)

dup_summary_by_facility(data_clean, fac_col_str, dup_group_ids)

dup_summary_overall(data_clean, group_counts, dup_groups)

Arguments

data

A data frame already passed through clean_names_safe().

facility_col, visit_col

Symbols for the resolved facility and visit columns.

order_by_quo

The captured order_by expression (a quosure from rlang::enquo()), possibly NULL.

keep

One of "first", "last", or "most_complete".

call

The environment errors are attributed to; see resolve_col().

fac_col_str, visit_col_str

Names of the facility and visit columns.

data_clean

A data frame already passed through clean_names_safe().

dup_group_ids

The .group_id values of the groups with more than one row.

group_counts

The data frame returned by count_visit_row_groups().

dup_groups

group_counts restricted to groups with n_rows > 1.

Value

sort_for_dedupe() returns data, sorted when order_by applies. keep_group_rows() returns the deduplicated data frame. count_visit_row_groups() returns a list with data (with a .group_id column) and counts. dup_summary_by_facility() and dup_summary_overall() return tibbles.

Details

dedupe() calls sort_for_dedupe() (apply the optional order_by, which keep = "most_complete" ignores with a warning) and then keep_group_rows() (apply the keep strategy within each facility x visit group).

summarize_duplicates() calls count_visit_row_groups() (one row per facility x visit group with its row count), dup_summary_by_facility(), and dup_summary_overall().

Grouping directly on facility_col/visit_col would follow the dplyr SQL-style convention of treating every NA as equal to every other NA, silently collapsing rows with a missing identifier into a single "duplicate" even though a missing value means the row's true identity is unknown, not confirmed to match. Both exported functions therefore group with na_safe_group_id(), which gives each NA-key row its own singleton group, and report how many rows were affected.

For keep = "most_complete", dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()) already excludes .group_id: dplyr::pick() never includes the active grouping variable(s) among the columns it can pick, so no explicit exclusion is needed (or possible, since pick() errors if asked to exclude a column it never included).
